title: Flow-control eviction layers and fidelity-mode switcher
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a multi-tier flow-control system that layers lightweight eviction strategies with a runtime 'fidelity-mode' switcher. Goal: preserve SLOs under transient and sustained overload by smoothly degrading output fidelity and admission, reducing tail latency and error budget burn while minimizing customer-visible failures. This ticket covers: 1) an eviction stack (fast token eviction, soft-trim, deferred-resume) to quickly reclaim memory/slots for hot-tenants; 2) an admission controller that applies probabilistic ticketing, per-tenant soft-quotas, and fast-path preemption; 3) a fidelity-mode switcher to change response modes per-tenant/route (full, compact, summary-only, deny) with runtime flags and safe rollback; 4) integration with regional circuit-breakers and multi-region failover policies so fidelity changes are coordinated across regions; 5) metrics, dashboards, and an automated rollout plan with canary percentages tied to error-budget burn. This approach focuses on minimizing user visible 'hard failures' by preferring graded degradation (shorter outputs, lower sampling, cached responses, structured placeholders) before outright rejecting requests. Key trade-offs: complexity of mode manager vs reduced rate of high-severity incidents; extra runtime state vs lower tail latency. Implementation will be staged: prototype in canary fleet, benchmark under synthetic spike, iterate on thresholds, then region-wide gradual rollout with manual guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype eviction layers deployed to canary fleet and demonstrating >= 35% reduction in memory-induced OOMs under bursty workloads
Admission controller enforces per-tenant soft-quotas and probabilistic admission with configurable thresholds via console
Fidelity-mode switcher can toggle modes per-route with zero-schema changes and preserves response validity for existing clients
SLO preservation: under sustained 2x traffic without capacity increase, 90th latency increases by <= 1.5x and P99 reduces error-rate compared to baseline rejection strategy
Automated dashboard shows error-budget burn correlation with mode switches and circuit-breaker trips
Runbook updated with step-by-step recovery (mode rollback, tenant pinning, regional fallback), and on-call run-through passed in tabletop exercise
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial spec drafted. Primary objective is to reduce hard reject rate by favoring progressive degradation. Proposed four fidelity modes and three eviction layers. Plan to reuse existing token-bucket counters and add a lightweight per-request admission stamp.

2026-03-11 Marcus Li: Reviewed design. Requested clarification on how fidelity-mode interacts with model-variant fallback (quantized vs full). Decided fidelity-mode is orthogonal: it mutates response generation parameters (max tokens, sampling temperature, output filters) while model-fallback remains a separate routing decision.

2026-03-11 Design feedback (Ivy Chen): Need clear UX signals in Console when a tenant is in degraded mode. Suggest adding per-route banners and an audit log entry for each mode switch. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12 Engineering note (Marcus Li): Implemented eviction-stack prototype: fast token eviction (O(1) evict oldest prefixes), soft-trim (truncate oversized requests early), deferred-resume (queue until token budget reclaimed). Benchmarks on canary show 38% reduction in OOM events during a synthetic spike scenario.

2026-03-12 Reliability (Diego Ramos): Circuite-breaker tie-in documented: when cross-region error budget burn > 30% in < 10 minutes, mode switcher will escalate the affected tenants to 'compact' automatically and notify SRE paging policy. Need to refine thresholds.

2026-03-13 QA (Rina Kaur): Test plan added for API backwards compatibility. Verified that clients using structured output via function-calling receive schema-compliant placeholders when in 'summary-only' mode.

2026-03-13 Marcus Li: Next steps: add per-tenant telemetry (mode history), wire Console toggles, write automated experiments for gradual rollout, and schedule tabletop with on-call team before regional rollout. Assigned follow-ups to ENG-720421 (console toggles) and ENG-720422 (telemetry pipeline).
runbook_summary: If error-budget burn spikes and mode switcher escalates: 1) check canary metrics dashboard; 2) pin affected tenants to 'compact' mode via emergency toggle; 3) if instability persists, enable regional fallback to secondary region and notify on-call; 4) after stabilization, roll back changes and open RCA. Include links to audit log and tenant mode history for postmortem.
